verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents a remote-access path: it tries peer-to-peer first and falls back to a relay, and you can use RustDesk's public rendezvous/relay or self-host one with a compose.yml. A long-time user confirms it works away from home without opening ports or a VPN when running their own relay. The documented path is thin, though: the pack has only brief statements and one setup step, no port-forward, direct-IP or VPN guidance, and some users report slow default servers and connection difficulties. missing for 10: detailed relay/self-host setup documentation (ports, firewall, client configuration), documented port-forward or direct-IP path, VPN guidance, consistent hands-on corroboration of reliable off-network connections.

support.subject: As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented

citations.quote: clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
No need to open ports, no need for vpn, it just works
